name: Phases of Play
content:
In Renaissance, each campaign progresses by cycling through three phases: PREMESSA, QUEST, and INTERMEZZO. Throughout the course of these phases, the GM will occasionally be called upon to make SOFT MOVES and HARD MOVES, which serve to introduce challenges for the players to overcome.

PREMESSA

The PREMESSA is the introduction or prelude to a Quest.

The GM sets the initial scene and introduces the object of the Quest. The object of the Quest should be unambiguous, and the party should have enough information at the outset to determine at least an initial course of action in the pursuit of that object.

From the players, we should learn why and how each character has joined the Quest, and we should get an initial taste of the dynamics between the party members. Why are you here? Do you know each other? Has the party been hired by someone or have other forces compelled them to take up the Quest? What are the stakes? Are there any NPCs along for the ride?

You should also determine the Quest's Keeping during the Premessa (see the Treasure & Keeping section).

It’s important to note that, at the outset of a Quest, we are exploring why each character has joined the quest, not whether they will join. By bringing a character to the game session, the player is making the decision that that character wants to participate in the Quest (though the character themselves may have reservations).

Depending on whether you’ve already introduced the characters and other relevant information about the campaign world in previous Quests, this phase may be as brief as a few minutes or as long as a whole session. However long your Premessa is, it should answer two questions: "Who are we as a party?" and "What are we trying to do?" Once those are established, you're ready to enter the Quest phase.

ALTERNATE APPROACH: If the group wants to start the Quest in media res, the Premessa can consist of a discussion/recap of how the party got to the current moment in the Quest so you can jump right into the action. You should still aim to answer the questions "Who are we as a party?" and "What are we trying to do?"

QUEST

The QUEST is the main phase of the game. We are zoomed-in on our heroes and are watching their every move.

The GM describes the environment and introduces challenges for the characters to overcome on their path toward the object of the Quest. The players choose what actions their characters take to try to overcome those challenges, making dice rolls as dictated by the rules or as requested by the GM.

This phase ends when the object of the Quest is achieved or the party chooses to abandon the Quest. Either way, when the Quest concludes, we enter the Intermezzo phase:

INTERMEZZO

The time spent between Quests is an INTERMEZZO. Depending on your group’s preference and the available session time, an Intermezzo can serve as a coda to a Quest, a preamble to the next Quest, or even a standalone session between Quests.

At a minimum, an Intermezzo should cover the activities of the characters who participated in the last Quest in its immediate aftermath and/or the characters who will be participating in the next Quest.

Optionally, you may also check in on characters whose activities in the campaign world are occurring outside the scope of the previous and following Quests. During an Intermezzo, the distinction between "active" and "inactive" characters dissolves, and the group can check in on any characters as desired. Note that the activities of NPCs can also be included here in addition to player characters.

Depending on what's happening in the campaign, an Intermezzo may cover days, weeks, months or even years of in-world time. Characters may stick together or split up. They may stay put or travel far and wide. This is a time to grow and enrich characters’ connections to the world around them, investigate curious places or rumors, add campaign questions to your list or even discover some answers, as the group deems appropriate.

There are also specific, mechanical actions characters can take to heal and recover during an Intermezzo. See the Rest & Recovery section.

Note that there is no GM during an Intermezzo. The group collectively holds the power and duties of the GM and adjudication is only done by finding group consensus.

During this phase, depending on what players choose to do, the group may call for and interpret the outcome of rolls, reward actions or impose consequences. Also note that players continue to have sovereignty over the characters under their care, even if they haven’t actively played them in a while.

You may also opt to establish some sort of above-the-table tradition to mark each Intermezzo. For example, you might make a round of toasts to celebrate the completion of a Quest and the prospect of a new one (in echo of the characters themselves sitting around a table in a tavern enjoying some hard-earned comfort).

An Intermezzo can be a quick roundup or montage, detailed roleplay scenes, somewhere in between, or a mix of all. Choose whatever helps you tell a compelling story. Discuss what kind of Intermezzo you want to create and dive in.

Always end an Intermezzo by discussing and choosing the next Quest as a group. Review your list of campaign questions, remove any that have been answered or no longer interest the group, add any questions that have come up, and, finally, choose which question(s) you want to answer with the next Quest and identify who will be the GM for that Quest.

Once the next GM is chosen, it's up to them to determine exactly how to turn the question(s) into a Quest premise. Because there may be a fair bit of interpretation or creative license involved in turning questions into a Quest premise, the GM should propose at least a broad outline of the premise and get the group's consent to proceed. Once that's sorted, you're ready to begin a new cycle with another Premessa phase!
